tagline: A few high miles along the rim of the painted cliffs.
intro: SR-148 leaves the Cedar Mountain highway in a meadow and climbs through the Dixie National Forest, staying between 9,900 and 10,500 feet. At the monument entrance it turns sharply east and the speed limit drops, then it swings north past the visitor center on the rim and runs on to meet SR-143.

Below the rim the ground falls more than 2,000 feet into an amphitheater three miles across, colored by iron and manganese, which Native people called the Circle of Painted Cliffs. Settlers called country like this breaks, and added cedar for the junipers, which are not cedars.
season: The meadows are known for wildflowers in July and early August and for fall color in late September.

moments.title: Cedar Breaks Visitor Center
moments.text: A two-room log cabin that the Civilian Conservation Corps built on the rim in 1937, its peeled log ends cut to tapered buttresses.

moments.title: Alpine Pond
moments.text: One of the subalpine meadows that dot the rim, reached by an easy trail from the road, in high country where some bristlecone pines have stood more than 1,600 years.

practical: The road generally closes from mid-November through late May and becomes a groomed trail for snowmobiles, cross-country skiing and snowshoeing.
